title: Day-Zero Role Shadowing & Urgent Scope Eviction Protocol
creator: Maya Singh
description:
Purpose: Provide a compact, executable playbook for the first 72 hours of a product cycle (day-zero through day-three) that reduces onboarding friction, guarantees coverage for critical paths, and defines a clear, auditable process for urgent scope eviction when headcount or external blockers force cuts.

Summary: This protocol combines a lightweight role-shadowing schedule, a cross-team reserve matrix (who can swing in for which functional area), and a three-step scope-eviction decision flow (detect -> triage -> evict/replace) with templates for comms, acceptance gating, and fallbacks. It is intended for use when a cycle starts and immediate changes are required due to hiring delays, sudden engineering capacity loss, or high-priority enterprise requests.

Scope: Product, Eng, Design, QE, and Solutions Engineering. Not intended to replace long-term portfolio decisions; this is a time-boxed operational tool for the first cycle window and emergency mid-cycle snaps.

Outcome: Faster time-to-stability on day-zero, fewer blocked critical-path tasks after unexpected losses, clear ownership for cuts, and metrics to inform post-cycle retrospective decisions.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Role-shadowing rotation template populated and validated by at least two PMs and two Eng leads
A2: Cross-functional reserve matrix published to Confluence with named backups for top 8 critical initiatives
A3: Scope-eviction decision flow documented with sign-off authority list and communication templates
A4: A dry-run tabletop completed with one simulated engineer drop and recorded lessons
A5: Dashboard widgets created listing active evictions and customer-facing blocker impact
